effect of a drag condition on a potential-energy-only question
examined_surface.model_scope: Constant supplied or named surface gravity; mass and length conversions; partial reader-condition audit.

cases.request: What is the potential energy change of a 750 g mass through -40 cm with gravity 2 m/s2?
cases.observed_behavior: {"status": "answered", "kind": "pe", "value": -0.6, "response": "The gravitational potential energy change is -0.6 J at g = 2 m/s^2 (constant gravity; mass 0.75 kg, signed height change -0.4 m)."}; reviewed outcome: right

cases.request: With gravity 0 m/s2, what is the weight of a 3 kg object?
cases.expected_boundary: Constant-field weight m*g with g=0 is zero.
cases.observed_behavior: {"status": "answered", "kind": "weight", "value": 0, "response": "The weight is about 0 N at g = 0 m/s^2 (W = m g = 3 kg x 0 m/s^2; the same as 0 kg would weigh on Earth)."}; reviewed outcome: right
cases.independent_check: Constant-field weight m*g with g=0 is zero.

cases.request: What is the potential energy of a 2 kg object lifted 3 m on Mars with drag?
cases.expected_boundary: For gravitational potential energy, the endpoints determine m*g*delta_h=2*3.71*3=22.26 J under the stated constant Mars surface-gravity model. Drag can change required applied work or impact speed, but does not prevent computing this potential-energy change.
cases.observed_behavior: {"status": "withheld", "kind": "unsupported_model", "value": null, "response": "The supplied conditions need a different physical model or an unambiguous gravity value and unit; I will not replace them with Earth or classical defaults."}; reviewed outcome: withheld_valid

current_unresolved_limits: Open: blanket drag guard withholds potential-energy changes whose gravitational component is determined by endpoints. Narrow the condition dependency per requested quantity; do not remove drag guards from impact-speed/time calculations.
Only these three request forms were independently examined here; projectile, kinetic-energy, force, power, pendulum-amplitude and other model boundaries remain outside this audit.
Arbitrary English interpretation and correctness of the finite named-body gravity table are not proved.
